paragraphs: In the morning, engineers enter the cleanroom to run equipment and track batches. At midday, they review data with the characterization team and adjust the process window. In the afternoon, they run atomic-scale simulations to validate a new structure. Before leaving, they calculate yield and cost and prepare for a review.

In one sentence: build devices at the nanoscale. The work includes defining structures, tuning processes, reviewing characterization, managing yield, running simulations, and driving mass production. It combines intellectual work with time in a cleanroom suit.
